title: HTML and text direction: basics
description: Five questions on page structure, HTTP status codes and writing CSS that works right-to-left.
source: Sample quiz shipped with QuizCraft, based on introductory HTML/CSS material.

questions.text: Which element marks the main heading of a page?
questions.explanation: A page has one <h1> for its main heading. <head> and <title> describe the document rather than its visible content, and <main> wraps the content without giving it a heading level.

options.text: The character encoding the browser should use
The direction the text runs in
The font the page should load

questions.explanation: It tells the browser to decode the bytes of the page as UTF-8. Without it, non-Latin text such as Arabic can arrive as boxes or question marks.

questions.text: Which HTTP status code means the page was not found?
questions.explanation: 404 means the server has no resource at that address. 200 is success, 301 is a permanent redirect and 403 means access was refused.

questions.text: Which attribute lets a line of text pick its own direction from its content?
questions.explanation: dir="auto" asks the browser to look at the first strong directional character and lay the line out accordingly, which is what mixed Arabic and English lines need.

questions.text: Which CSS property replaces margin-left in a layout that must work in both directions?
questions.explanation: margin-inline-start is the logical equivalent of margin-left: it follows the writing direction, so it becomes the right-hand margin in a right-to-left layout.
